- Immediate asks from your team: 1) controller/processor allocation in DPA, 2) subprocessors list and process for notifications, 3) breach notification timeline, and 4) retention/deletion controls for user PII.

Thanks, Ben — appreciated. A few clarifying questions from our privacy team after a quick skim:

> On Tue, 21 Jul 2026 at 15:10, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> > I've attached our current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) and the current subprocessors export (Redwood_Subprocessors_List.csv) for your legal/security review.

1) Controller vs Processor: Sycamore will be the controller for end-user data. We just need explicit language confirming Redwood acts solely as a processor for any end-user PII collected through our integration (and that processing is only per our documented instructions). Please point to the DPA section where this is stated or provide suggested language.

2) Subprocessors: The CSV shows current subprocessors, but we need clarity on the notification window and how consent/objection works for new subprocessors. What is the timeline for notice before Redwood engages a new subprocessor?

3) Breach notice: We require notification within 48 hours of confirmed data breach materially affecting Sycamore data. The DPA currently references "prompt" notice. Can Redwood confirm commitment to 48-hour notice (or propose acceptable language)?

4) Data residency & retention: Our data classification requires that certain PII remains in the us-east-1 region and be deleted within 90 days of request. Can you confirm support for region pinning and provide the retention/deletion process (including proof of deletion/audit logs)?

If Marissa can respond directly to these, that would be great. Happy to schedule a 30-min call if that speeds it up.

Thanks,
Priya
Privacy & Compliance Lead
Sycamore Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@sycamorehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications & next steps — Sycamore Health

Hi Priya — thanks for the detailed list. See responses/commitments below (high level); attached is a marked-up excerpt of the DPA with suggested language and a redline for subprocessors notification timing.

1) Controller/Processor: Section 1.1 of the attached DPA confirms Sycamore Health is the Controller and Redwood is the Processor. Proposed explicit language (added in redline): "Redwood shall process Personal Data only on documented instructions from Controller and shall not act as a Controller with respect to such Personal Data."

2) Subprocessors: We provide 30 days' notice before onboarding a new subprocessor and publish an up-to-date list at https://www.redwood.com/subprocessors. The attached CSV is a snapshot; we will send an automated notice to the technical contact and to your legal contact (as listed in the DPA). If you object within 14 days, we will work to propose alternatives or confirm mitigation. The redline adds the 30-day notice and 14-day objection window.

3) Breach notice: We commit to notifying you of confirmed security incidents that materially affect Sycamore data as soon as reasonably practicable and no later than 48 hours after confirmation of the incident (we cannot commit to 48 hours for discovery/confirmation of suspected incidents, but will update you within 48 hours of confirmation). The DPA redline clarifies "notification within 48 hours of confirmation of a breach materially affecting Controller data."

4) Data residency & retention: For Redwood Private (VPC) deployments, you can pin workloads to us-east-1. We support record-level deletion requests and provide Audit logs showing deletion actions. Standard process: submit deletion request (API or support ticket), we execute within 72 hours for production data (90 days for backups), and provide a deletion certificate and audit log export. We added the deletion SLA language to the DPA redline.

Next steps:
- See attached: Redwood_DPA_v3_MarkedUp.pdf (excerpt with comments) and Redwood_Subprocessors_List.csv (annotated).
- Ben: happy to take any contractual redlines from Sycamore's counsel; if they are limited to the items above we can likely accept with minor edits.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: [Redwood_DPA_v3_MarkedUp.pdf (application/pdf), Redwood_Subprocessors_List.csv (text/csv)]
